sections.h2: Two county seats, one set of taxes
sections.html:
St. Clair County has two seats, Ashville and Pell City. The far southern end of the Appalachians runs through the county from northeast to southwest, which made it hard to run from one side, so Pell City was added to serve the southeast. County business can happen in either town.

When you call about a tax record, ask which office handles your parcel and whether you need to come in person. Phone the Revenue Commissioner's office or check the county's own site before you drive anywhere.

St. Clair County is in central Alabama, in the Birmingham metro area, and Pell City is its largest city. It had 91,103 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 98,206 for 2025, after growing at every count since 1980. Of 37,775 housing units, 9.0 percent were vacant, and 81.2 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied. About 67.1 percent of residents live outside urban areas, so many sales involve acreage, wells or septic.

A tax bill depends on whether the house sits inside a city and which taxing districts apply, so go by the parcel and not the mailing town. Trussville and Leeds, for example, are mostly in other counties even though parts reach into this one.

Alabama property tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31. If a bill goes unpaid, the process runs on a fixed calendar.

DateWhat happens
October 1Taxes due
December 31Last day to pay without delinquency; also the deadline to report improvements
January 1Taxes become delinquent
FebruaryUnpaid accounts go to probate court
MarchCourt meets on the delinquent list
AprilDelinquent parcels are advertised
MayTax sale

Counties are not required to mail a notice. The Revenue Commissioner's office sends one as a courtesy, so a missing bill does not cancel the debt. If you own a St. Clair County house you have not visited in a while, call the office and ask what, if anything, is owed.

The assessed value comes from an appraised value. The state's example applies a 10 percent assessment rate to $100,000 to get $10,000 before the millage rate is applied. A bill rises when the millage rises or when the appraised value goes up through reappraisal or the market.

Every Alabama county reviews a quarter of its parcels each year under annual equalization, so each parcel gets a full review every four years. The state says this produces smaller yearly changes than the old four-year jumps.

If you build onto a house, sign a new assessment at the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31 for work finished by October 1. Additions, pools, remodeling, an added bath, deck, patio, carport or garage all count as reportable. Re-roofing and painting do not.

An owner-occupied single-family home on up to 160 acres can qualify, as long as the owner lived in it on the first day of the tax year. Owners over 65, permanently and totally disabled owners and blind owners are exempt from the state share of the tax, though county taxes can still be due. You apply at the local county office.

About 17.4 percent of county residents were 65 or older in 2020, so many owners fall in the age group. A family selling a parent's house should find out whether a claim was on file, since the state share of the bill depends on it. If you inherited a house from an owner who had an exemption, ask the office what you need to file in your own name.

sections.h2: Buying or selling: who pays the tax
sections.html:
A buyer should record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the Revenue Commissioner's office, bringing the deed. A bill may still carry the former owner's name, and whoever owns the property answers for the tax anyway.

Sellers should do three things before closing:

  • Ask which year's tax is paid and whether any balance remains.
  • Write into the contract who pays the current year's tax.
  • Report any address change to the county office in writing.

To contest a value, ask the Revenue Commissioner's office for the appeal form and deadline before you list the house, so a high assessment does not surprise a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Steps to sell with taxes owed
sections.html:
Selling with an unpaid balance is routine. Start by calling the Revenue Commissioner's office for the current-year amount and any older years. Ask for the figure in writing so the closing agent can use it.

At closing, the title company pays the county from your proceeds before you are paid, and the deed is recorded in the probate office afterward. Bring the deed or your last tax statement, a photo ID and any paperwork showing an exemption or a recent improvement. If the bill was mailed to an old address, give the office the new one in writing so later notices reach you.

A cash purchase does not change these tax steps. The house is bought as it stands, the taxes are cleared from proceeds, and the sale skips the wait for a buyer's lender appraisal.

Interstate 20 and Interstate 59 cross the county, along with U.S. 11, 78, 231 and 411 and several state routes. Logan Martin Lake and Horse Pens 40, a private park on Chandler Mountain, draw visitors and affect how lake and mountain properties are marketed. Public schools run through the St. Clair County School District, so name the district and the nearest town when you describe a house to a buyer.

faqs.q: When are St. Clair County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31. Unpaid bills can move to a probate court tax sale in May.

faqs.q: Why are there two county seats in St. Clair County?
faqs.a: Ashville and Pell City are both seats because the Appalachian terrain divides the county, and Pell City was added to serve the southeast side.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax if I never received a bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The revenue commissioner is not required to mail notices, and the owner is responsible whether or not a statement arrives.

faqs.q: Do I have to report improvements to my house?
faqs.a: Yes, for additions, new structures, pools, remodeling and similar work done by October 1. Sign a new assessment at the revenue commissioner's office by December 31. Re-roofing and painting do not need one.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a St. Clair County assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the County Revenue Commissioner's office for the form and the deadline.
